Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. England Women Under-19 are in a huddle near the ropes and they now make their way out in the middle. They are followed by the India Women Under-19 openers. Shafali Verma and Shweta Sehrawat will open the innings for India Women Under-19. Hannah L Baker will start the proceedings with the ball for England Women Under-19. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, India Women Under-19 will certainly be the happier side at the halfway mark and they look set to clinch the inaugural ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup title. On the other hand, England Women Under-19 have their backs against the wall and they need nothing short of a miraculous bowling effort to defend this total. Do we have a twist in this game? We will find out shortly. Back in a bit for the chase...

Titas Sadhu is in for a spot interview. She says that they had planned to give them good starts and focused on enjoying their game. Adds the surface was fast but a bit flat. Although there was some bounce on offer as well. Mentions they will try to keep it simple with the bat and get over the line here.

Having won the toss, India Women Under-19 set the tone early with the new ball and dealt early blows to the England Women Under-19. They kept the pressure on and did not allow the opposition batters to get going. India Women Under-19 kept chipping in with wickets at regular intervals throughout the innings. Moreover, their fielding was top notch and it backed up their bowling. Titas Sadhu, Archana Devi and Parshavi Chopra accounted for two wickets each while the trio of Mannat Kashyap, Sonam Yadav and Shafali Verma had a wicket each to their names.

WOW! India Women Under-19 completely outclassed England Women Under-19. This has been a complete domination by India Women Under-19 and they have bowled England Women Under-19 out for a paltry total of 68. Having been asked to bat first, England Women Under-19 were off to a poor start losing three wickets inside the Powerplay. They failed to recover from that start and were reduced to 39-5 inside 10 overs. Their batters failed to gather any momentum and kept perishing one after the other. Ryana Macdonald-Gay did show some resistance but she kept losing partners at the other end. Her dismissal meant England Women Under-19 failed get a competitive total on the board and they were bowled without playing the full quota of 20 overs.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! A dominating performance by India Women Under-19 with the ball comes to an end. It is tossed up, full and on off. Sophia Smale though tries to work it down the leg side but ends up chipping back to the bowler. Sonam Yadav takes a dolly and bundles England Women Under-19 for 68 runs.
Mannat Kashyap gives it a bit more flight this time, just outside off. Ellie Anderson dabs it out.
A dot now! Floated and full, outside off. Ellie Anderson is unable to get it through the gap in the off side.
Ellie Anderson is the last batter in for England Women Under-19.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mannat Kashyap comes back into the attack and finds the breakthrough. England Women Under-19 lose their ninth wicket now. It is a bit shorter, outside off. Alexa Stonehouse rocks back and throws the kitchen sink at it. She could not keep her shot under control and Sonam Yadav pouches it safely.
Commentary.Howout: c Sonam Yadav b Mannat Kashyap

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off. Alexa Stonehouse drives it hard to extra cover but not in the gap.
Slightly short and on off. Alexa Stonehouse punches it to cover. The fielder there dives to her right and parries it past extra cover. Two taken.
Floats it up, full and on the stumps. Alexa Stonehouse makes some room, and bunts it out to the off side.
Mannat Kashyap (2-0-11-0) comes back on, replacing Shafali Verma.
Alexa Stonehouse slices this full ball from outside off to sweeper cover. They only get a single here.
Full and outside off. Alexa Stonehouse gets it to backward point off the outer half.
On off, pushed to the off side for one.
A flighted ball, full and on off. Alexa Stonehouse miscues it towards extra cover but it evades the flying fielder. One taken.
Slower one, on off, it gets some extra bounce off it. Alexa Stonehouse pushes it to the off side.
This is tossed up, angled in, just outside off. It grips and turns away. Alexa Stonehouse leaves it alone.
So, 10 runs and a wicket off the over. It is a flatter ball, on off. Smale gets a thick insdie edge on it. The ball goes through the legs of Richa Ghosh. They take two.
FOUR! Sophia Smale gets her second boundary of the over. It is a flighted ball, going down leg. Smale tickles it down to fine leg for four runs.
Much fuller and on off. Smale presses forward and blocks it away.
On off, defended out.

FOUR! This is darted on the pads. Smale flicks it aerially past square leg. There are shouts of catch but it evades the fielder and has enough legs to reach the fence. Sophia Smale is off with a boundary.
Sophia Smale is the new batter in.

OUT! STUMPED! Sharp work by Richa Ghosh behind the sticks! Shafali Verma tosses this one full and outside off, Hannah L Baker gets tempted and looks to get on the front foot. Fails to get any bat as she tried to defend and drags her foot out of the crease. Richa Ghosh behind the wicket takes the bails off in a flash and catches Hannah L Baker inches out of her crease.
Commentary.Howout: st Richa Ghosh b Shafali Verma

Commentary.Commentary: Is this stumped? The square leg umpire goes upstairs. Richa Ghosh is very confident. It is a legal delivery and to make it worse for England the decision goes in favour of India Women Under-19, as Hannah L Baker has nothing inside the crease.
Fuller delivery and on leg, Alexa Stonehouse blocks this one out on the leg side.
Hannah L Baker gets a promotion in the batting order and comes out at number 9.

OUT! RUN OUT! Another one bites the dust! This is disastrous for England Women Under-19! Parshavi Chopra bowls this one slower and short on off, Josie Groves goes back in her crease and punches this one along the ground on the off side. Sonam Yadav at cover fumbles initially but recovers well and fires in a throw at the non-striker's end. She hits and catches Josie Groves out of her crease. India Women Under-19 continue to inflict more misery on England Women Under-19 with their brilliant fielding.

Is that a run out? The umpire takes it upstairs to confirm. India Women Under-19 players have already started celebrating and they do not have to stop their celebration here as the third umpire confirms that it is OUT.
Short and quicker on off, Alexa Stonehouse taps this one on the off side and takes a quick single.

DROPPED! Archana Devi has shelled it! Floated, fuller around off, Alexa Stonehouse steps out of her crease and drives it uppishly towards extra cover. Archana Devi dives forward but the ball pops out of her hands.
Parshavi Chopra fires this one full and at the pads, Alexa Stonehouse shapes to play this one on the leg side but gets into a tangle and cannot get it away.
Short and on off, Alexa Stonehouse rocks back and punches this one off the back foot but fails to get it through the infield.
Flatter at the stumps, Alexa Stonehouse pushes this one uppishly but wide of mid-wicket for a single.
Some more turn! Short and on off, the ball turns sharply into the batter, Alexa Stonehouse shapes to cut this one but misses.
Short and on off, Alexa Stonehouse pushes this one back to the bowler from the crease.

FOUR! Nicely played! Shafali Verma bowls this one full on off, Alexa Stonehouse picks the length early and drives this one down the ground. Gets it past the diving fielder at mid off for a boundary. 50 comes up for England Women Under-19. It comes belatedly but they will surely take it.
A bit short around off, Alexa Stonehouse pushes this one on the off side but fails to get it past cover.
Shafali Verma starts with a fuller delivery at the pads, Josie Groves clips this one towards deep square leg and takes a single.
Change. Shafali Verma now gets herself into the attack.
Loopy ball, on off, defended out watchfully.
Alexa Stonehouse is cramped for room here as this is pushed through quicker and on off. Alexa Stonehouse defends it out to point.
A single now as this is pushed to covers.
Floated and full, outside off. Groves flicks towards wide long on. The fielders in the deep work in tandem to keep it down to two. India Women Under-19 have been excellent in the field today.
Flighted, fuller around off, Josie Groves gets on the front foot and drives this along the ground to extra cover.
Josie Groves walks in at number 8. She scored precious 15 runs in the semi-final. Will she be able to add some impetus to the total here?

OUT! CAUGHT! Archana Devi has taken a stunner here! Parshavi Chopra flights this one nicely, fuller on off, Ryana Macdonald-Gay shimmies down the track and looks to drive this one on the off side. Ends up chipping this one uppishly towards extra cover. Archana Devi there dives full length to her right and takes an excellent one-handed catch. England Women Under-19 slip further as they are now 6 down.
Commentary.Howout: c Archana Devi b Parshavi Chopra

Commentary.Commentary: Short and slower on off, Alexa Stonehouse taps this one off the back foot to cover.
Short and quicker on off, Alexa Stonehouse punches this one off the back foot to cover.
Sharp turn! Short and turning away on off, Alexa Stonehouse looks to cut this one on the off side but gets beaten by the sharp away turn.
Floated, fuller on off, Ryana Macdonald-Gay shuffles across and drives it uppishly towards cover for a single.
Tossed up, full around off, Alexa Stonehouse clears her front leg to go down the ground but gets a thickish outside edge that flies uppishly towards backward point. The batters cross for a single.

NO BALL! Mannat Kashyap bowls this one short and on off, Ryana Macdonald-Gay steps out and pushes this one towards extra cover for a single. Mannat Kashyap has overstepped and a Free Hit will follow now.
Short and turning away outside off, near the tramline, Ryana Macdonald-Gay reaches out to the delivery but fails to get any bat on it.

Drinks Break! With England Women Under-19 tottering at 39-5, India Women Under-19 are well on top at the moment. However, they cannot afford to relax and must look to keep chipping in with wickets at regular intervals. On the other hand, England Women Under-19 need Ryana Macdonald-Gay to bat through along with support from the lower order. They would be hoping to reach the 100-run mark which would give them something to bowl at.

OUT! LBW! Parshavi Chopra gets herself into the wicket's column now. England Women Under-19 have half of their side back in the hut within the first half of the first innings. It is a bit fuller, on off. Charis Pavely gets down on one knee and goes for the sweep but misses it completely. She takes a blow on her pads. Parshavi Chopra puts in an appeal and this time the umpire agrees to India Women Under-19's delight.
Full and outside off. Ryana Macdonald-Gay pushes it to extra cover and crosses.

An appeal for lbw but turned down! Richa Ghosh informs that if it was a bit fuller then the umpire migth've raised the finger. It is flighted, full and on middle. Ryana Macdonald-Gay tries to flick it away but ends up playing all around it. She gets pinged on her pads but the umpire thinks it is going above the wicket.
A googly this time. Ryana Macdonald-Gay picks it up very late but manages to defend it out.
Direct hit could've been curtains for Charis Pavely. It is full and on off. Pavley whips it to mid on. Shafali Verma's throw at the non-striker's end is wayard and Pavely makes it safely for one.
This is full and on leg. Ryana Macdonald-Gay nudges it through the leg side for a single.
Shortish, outside off. Ryana Macdonald-Gay cuts it to backward point and crosses. 7 runs off the over but most importantly without losing any wicket.
Around off, defended off the front foot.
FOUR! Ryana Macdonald-Gay is getting into her groove here. It is full and on off. Ryana Macdonald-Gay uses fer feet and thumps it down the ground for a cracking boundary.
On off, pushed to the off side for a single.

A loud shout for lbw but turned down! It is looped up, around off, it turns in off the deck. Charis Pavely is a bit early into her sweep shot and takes a hit on her pads. The umpire is not interested. It might be going down leg.
It is floated and full, on off. Ryana Macdonald-Gay drives it to the right of mid off and takes off.
Spin from both ends as Mannat Kashyap comes on to bowl.
Floated and full, around off, angled across. Charis Pavely tries to block it away but does so inside the line. Parshavi Chopra goes for 6 runs in her first over.
Flighted and full, on middle. Ryana Macdonald-Gay flicks it through the gap at mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! A much-needed boundary for England Women Under-19. It is pushed through quicker, full and outside off. Ryana Macdonald-Gay frees her arms and slashes it past backward point for four runs.
Full and on off, defended out.
WIDE! Chopra spills it down leg. Ryana Macdonald-Gay tries to sweep it fine but does not connect. Wide called.
Around of defended back to the bowler.
England Women Under-19 have their task cut out against the leg spin of Parshavi Chopra.
Loopy ball, full and on off. pushed out to safety.
Three dots on the trot to end the over! Charis Pavely drives this full ball into covers. The fielder there dives to her right and makes a sharp stop to restrict a single.
On off, blocked back to the bowler.
No run. A slower length ball, in the channel. Charis Pavely keeps her bat to herself. The ball dies as it reaches the keeper.

WIDE! A loosener this by Sadhu but she can be forgiven for this minor error. It is a short ball, wide of off, shaping away. Charis Pavely looks to chase it but misses. The umpire signals a wide as the ball goes past the tramline.
A bit fuller, outside off. Pavely shuffles across and makes a good leave. So ofcourse there are some nerves involved now.
Charis Pavely walks in at number 6 with her side reeling at 22-4.

OUT! TIMBER! England Women Under-19 are falling like a deck of cards here. This is going from bad to wrose for the English side here. Titas Sadhu gets her second wicket. It is a peach of a delivery, on a length, that lands outside off and jags back in. Seren Smale tries to defend it away but gets beaten by the inside edge. The ball sneaks through the gap between bat and pad to rattle the stumps.  Seren Smale once again attacks the ball without moving her feet and pays the price this time.
Titas Sadhu steams in and dishes a length ball, on fifth stump. Smale defends it to cover without any feet movement. This is dangerous batting.

Archana Devi sees the batter charge down the wicket and serves it full and wide outside off. Ryana Macdonald-Gay has to make a late adjustment to reach far and wide outside off. She is just able to stab it away. At the end of Powerplay, England Women Under-19 are teetering at 22/3.
Around off, blocked out watchfully.
FOUR! This should settle some nerves. Ryana Macdonald-Gay gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over mid off for four runs. A rare sight for the English fans.
Short again, but this time some width on offer. Ryana Macdonald-Gay cuts it to backward point but straight to the fielder.
Devi drags her length ball, on middle. Smale swivels and pulls it to deep mid-wicket. There is protection in the deep and they only get a single.
Loopy ball, on off, defended out.
Full and outside off, Ryana Macdonald-Gay gets forward and drives it straight to cover.

DROPPED! Titas Sadhu pitches this one full and outside off, Ryana Macdonald-Gay goes for the drive away from the body. Ends up getting an outside edge that flies behind the wicket towards the keeper. Richa Ghosh dives to her right but fails to hang onto it.
Short of a length outside off, Ryana Macdonald-Gay looks to cut this one hard on the off side but connects with thin air.

Sloppy stuff! Titas Sadhu continues to bowl it into the wicket and bowls it on off, Seren Smale punches this one back to the bowler. Titas Sadhu fumbles in her follow-through and there is no one to back her up. The English batters sneak in a single as the ball rolls towards mid off.
Short of a length outside off, Seren Smale stays on the back foot and punches it straight to cover.
Titas Sadhu bowls this one back of a length outside off, Seren Smale hangs back to cut this one on the off side but gets it from the bottom part of the bat towards cover.
Ryana Macdonald-Gay is the new batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Archana Devi goes BANG,BANG and it is all smiles for India Women Under-19. It is tossed up, on off. Grace Scrivens dances down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it down the ground. Although, Grace Scrivens is unable to get a good connection on it. The ball does not get enough distance on it as she would've envisioned. Gongadi Trisha charges in from long off and takes a sharp catch diving forward. England Women Under-19 are in a spot of bother here.
Commentary.Howout: c Gongadi Trisha b Archana Devi

Commentary.Commentary: Gives it some air this time, full, on middle and leg. Smale flicks it to mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single here.
Devi goes full and outside off. Smale prods and defends it out.
Seren Smale is the new batter at the crease. The England wicket-keeper has her task cut out.

OUT! TIMBER! Nicely tossed up, fuller on off, Niamh Holland gets inside the line of the ball to paddle this one fine on the leg side. The ball spins sharply past the inside edge and she ends up missing it altogether. The ball takes the off stump and India Women Under-19 are delighted. This was a proper off-spinners dismissal by Archana Devi.
Floats it up, full and on off. Niamh Holland hangs back and dabs it to the off side.

FOUR! Archana Devi continues to float this one, full outside off, Niamh Holland gets down and sweeps this one through backward square leg. Hrishita Basu performs the chase but fails to keep the ball in and concedes a boundary.
WIDE! Archana Devi sees the batter shuffle and bowls it short but just outside the tramline on the off side. Niamh Holland leaves it alone and the umpire signals a wide.
Length delivery outside off, Grace Scrivens slashes hard the delivery but the ball keeps a bit low and she fails to get any bat on it.
Another fuller delivery outside off, Grace Scrivens goes for a waft away from her body but fails to connect.

Titas Sadhu pitches this one full on off, Grace Scrivens drives this one firmly towards extra cover. Hrishita Basu there dives to her right but ends up parrying it away from the mid off fielder. That allows the batters to run two.
Fuller and outside off, Grace Scrivens pushes this one towards mid off for a dot.
Back of a length and on leg, a hint of inward movement, Grace Scrivens looks to turn this one on the leg side but gets cramped for room.

Good stop! Titas Sadhu bowls this one a bit short outside off, Niamh Holland uses her feet and cuts this one towards backward point. Mannat Kashyap dives to her left and makes a good diving stop. The batters cross for a single.
Flighted delivery, full around off, Grace Scrivens drives this one a bit uppishly towards Shafali Verma at extra cover.
Floated, full and at the stumps, Grace Scrivens pushes this one to the right of the bowler. Archana Devi goes after the ball in her follow-through and denies a single.
Slower and short outside off, Niamh Holland shuffles across and plays it with the turn. Pulls it along the ground to deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Niamh Holland is up and running! Short and turning into the batter on off, Niamh Holland cuts hard at the delivery but gets an outside edge that travels past the first slip fielder for a boundary.
Slower and short, turning away outside off, Grace Scrivens knocks this one down to long off and takes a single.
Archana Devi starts with a flighted delivery, a bit short outside off, Grace Scrivens punches this one off the back foot to cover.

A slightly new approach from India, rather than getting on a leg spinner, Shafali Verma opts for Archana Devi's threat of off spin to put England Women Under-19 under the pump here. Can Archana Devi find a breakthrough in her first over?
Shortish delivery outside off, Niamh Holland reaches out and slashes at the delivery but fails to get any bat on it.
Fuller outside off, Niamh Holland drives this one to the left of the bowler for a dot.

Niamh Holland comes in at number 3. Well she has to come out a bit early than what she would've anticipated. Will she be able to stitch a solid stand with her skipper and take her side to safer shores?

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Titas Sadhu strikes and India Women Under-19 draw first blood! Titas Sadhu bangs this one into the wicket at the batter, Liberty Heap tries to pull this one from the crease but is in no position to execute the shot. Ends up lobbing this towards the bowler and Titas Sadhu does the rest.
Back of a length outside off, Liberty Heap looks to punch this one but toe-ends it to cover.
On a fuller length outside off, Grace Scrivens drives this one along the ground towards backward point. A half-stop there allows the batters to cross for a single.
Titas Sadhu starts with a back-of-a-length delivery outside off from 'round the wicket, Grace Scrivens pushes this one to cover for a dot.

Well, we are done with all the pre-match proceedings. Both the teams shakes hands before the battle it out for the U-19 Women's World Cup trophy. The India players are seen to be in a huddle. Shafali Verma is heard saying that they need to give 100% on the field but majorly focus on enjoying themselves. It is all about the start in the shortest format and to give England Women Under-19 a solid platform, it is Grace Scrivens and Liberty Heap who walk out to open for them. Titas Sadhu will be starting with the new ball.

Right then, the time has come that everyone has been waiting for. Both the teams are seen making their way out in the middle for their respective national anthems. It will be England's anthem first followed by the Indian national anthem.

England Women Under-19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Grace Scrivens (C), Liberty Heap, Niamh Holland, Seren Smale (WK), Charis Pavely, Ryana Macdonald-Gay, Alexa Stonehouse, Josie Groves, Ellie Anderson, Sophia Smale, Hannah L Baker.

India Women Under-19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Shweta Sehrawat, Shafali Verma (C), Soumya Tiwari, Gongadi Trisha, Richa Ghosh (WK), Hrishita Basu, Titas Sadhu, Mannat Kashyap, Archana Devi, Parshavi Chopra, Sonam Yadav.

After two weeks of exhilarating action that saw 16 teams battle it out for cricket supremacy, only two are left with a chance to create history by winning the inaugural Women’s U-19 T20 World Cup. India Women Under-19 and England Women Under-19, the first-ever finalists of the tournament, will lock horns in what is expected to be a blockbuster summit clash in Potchefstroom. India’s dominant performance against New Zealand in the first semi-final saw them secure one of the final berths, while England had to dig deep to win a low-scoring thriller against a strong Australian side. Going into the final, India would hope for a better contribution with the bat from their skipper Shafali Verma, who has blown hot and cold throughout the tournament, and would also hope that their spinners continue their good form with the ball and choke England's run flow at a pitch that is expected to aid them. The standout performer with the bat for them has been Shweta Sehrawat, with 292 runs, and she is the highest run-scorer in the tournament so far. Parshavi Chopra has been their top performer with the ball, with nine wickets and Mannat Kashyap is not far behind with eight scalps. They would have seen that the English batters struggled against spin in the semi-final and will look to use it to their advantage. They will want to put their best foot forward and make billions of people proud. England, on the other hand, have had a perfect tournament so far, and they are coming into the final undefeated. However, they suffered a scare in the semi-final when they were bowled out for just 99 runs, but they showed great resilience and fought back to get over the line by just three runs. Hannah L Baker was the key performer with the ball who also has nine wickets to her name so far, while skipper Grace Scrivens also contributed and she has taken eight wickets. She is also the second-highest run scorer with 289 runs, and it will be a good battle to see between her and Shweta Sehrawat as to who finishes as the top scorer. After winning a game like that, it will give them immense confidence in getting their hands on the trophy against a strong Indian side. The weather is expected to be clear, and the spinners from both teams will be important as we have seen turn on this pitch, and it is not easy to bat on. Both sides look well-matched, and it is hard to pick a winner. These two teams have the chance to create history, and we are surely in for an exciting final. Whose side are you on?
